quick: INR with warfarin; LFTs if symptoms
summary: Ranitidine is a competitive, reversible H2-receptor antagonist that suppresses gastric acid secretion, used for duodenal and gastric ulcers, GERD, erosive esophagitis, and pathological hypersecretory states such as Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. It was withdrawn from the US and most global markets in 2020 at FDA request due to NDMA (nitrosamine) contamination concerns and is no longer marketed.
indications: Short-term treatment of active duodenal ulcer (most heal within 4 weeks)
Maintenance therapy of duodenal ulcer at reduced dosage after healing
Pathological hypersecretory conditions (e.g. Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, systemic mastocytosis)
Short-term treatment of active benign gastric ulcer (most heal within 6 weeks)
Maintenance therapy of gastric ulcer at reduced dosage after healing
Treatment of endoscopically diagnosed erosive esophagitis
Maintenance of healing of erosive esophagitis

dosage.d: 150 mg twice daily, or 300 mg once daily after the evening meal or at bedtime
dosage.n: Antacid may be given as needed for pain

dosage.d: 150 mg twice daily; titrate to need, dosed more frequently if required
dosage.t: Continue as long as clinically indicated
dosage.n: Doses up to 6 g/day used in severe disease
Maintenance of healing: 150 mg twice daily

dosage.t: Frequency may increase to q12h with caution if needed
dosage.n: Time dose to coincide with end of hemodialysis

admin: Take orally with or without food (absorption not significantly impaired by food or antacids)
Concomitant antacids may be given as needed for pain relief
Adjust dose in renal impairment; for hemodialysis patients, schedule dosing at the end of dialysis
Product contains FD&C Yellow No. 5 (tartrazine), which may cause allergic-type reactions in susceptible persons
moa: Ranitidine is a competitive, reversible inhibitor of histamine at the H2-receptors of gastric parietal cells, reducing basal and stimulated gastric acid secretion and acid volume. It is not anticholinergic and does not lower serum calcium in hypercalcemic states.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to ranitidine or any ingredient
History of acute porphyria (may precipitate attacks)
relative: Tartrazine (FD&C Yellow No. 5) sensitivity, frequently with aspirin hypersensitivity
monitor: Symptomatic response does not exclude gastric malignancy - investigate alarm features
Monitor INR/prothrombin time with concomitant warfarin
Monitor for procainamide toxicity at ranitidine doses >300 mg/day

preg: Pregnancy category not established in the provided prescription label; data are limited. Historically considered relatively low-risk and used in pregnancy, but the product was withdrawn in 2020 and is no longer marketed. Avoid use; consider currently approved acid-suppressing alternatives.
lact: Ranitidine is excreted in human milk. Exercise caution if a nursing mother requires therapy; product is no longer marketed, so use approved alternatives.
renal: Reduce dose in renal impairment: for creatinine clearance <50 mL/min, give 150 mg every 24 hours; frequency may be cautiously increased to every 12 hours if needed. Time dosing to the end of hemodialysis, which lowers circulating ranitidine.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic dysfunction since ranitidine is metabolized in the liver; compensated cirrhosis causes only minor, clinically insignificant pharmacokinetic changes. Discontinue immediately if hepatitis develops.

major: Warfarin (altered prothrombin time - monitor INR closely)
moderate: Procainamide and N-acetylprocainamide (reduced renal excretion at ranitidine doses >300 mg/day)
Ketoconazole (decreased absorption due to raised gastric pH)
minor: Propantheline (delays and increases peak ranitidine levels)
interactions.food: Absorption not significantly impaired by food.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; it can aggravate acid-related disease and gastric irritation.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine protein with MULTISTIX; use sulfosalicylic acid testing instead. Discontinue before histamine skin-allergy testing to avoid false-negative results.

serious: Hepatocellular, cholestatic, or mixed hepatitis (rarely hepatic failure)
Blood dyscrasias: leukopenia, granulocytopenia, thrombocytopenia; rarely agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, aplastic anemia
Cardiac arrhythmias (tachycardia, bradycardia, AV block, premature ventricular beats)
rare: Reversible mental confusion, agitation, depression, hallucinations (especially severely ill elderly)
emergency: Acute porphyric attack in susceptible patients

monitoring: INR/prothrombin time when co-administered with warfarin
Liver function if symptoms or signs of hepatitis arise (discontinue immediately)
Complete blood count if signs of blood dyscrasia
Renal function to guide dose adjustment
Procainamide levels/toxicity at ranitidine doses >300 mg/day
Reassessment for gastric malignancy in patients with persistent symptoms
counsel: Take as directed; may be taken with or without food
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, or persistent abdominal pain (possible liver effects)
Persistent or worsening symptoms warrant further evaluation - do not assume relief excludes serious disease
Tell your provider about all medicines, especially warfarin
Note: ranitidine was recalled and withdrawn from the market in 2020 due to NDMA contamination - discuss alternatives with your provider
pearls: Ranitidine was withdrawn from the US and most global markets in 2020 at FDA request after NDMA (a probable human carcinogen / nitrosamine) was found to accumulate in the product, especially over time and at higher temperatures; it is no longer marketed and this record is for reference only.
Oral bioavailability is about 50%; ~30% of an oral dose is excreted unchanged in urine with renal clearance (~410 mL/min) indicating active tubular secretion - the basis for renal dose reduction.
A weaker CYP450 inhibitor than cimetidine and, unlike cimetidine, does not cause gynecomastia or impotence.
Avoid in acute porphyria - it may precipitate attacks.
Symptomatic response does not rule out gastric malignancy; investigate alarm features (weight loss, bleeding, dysphagia).
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up. (Note: the product is withdrawn and no longer available.)
overdose: Experience is limited; acute ingestions up to 18 g have caused transient effects similar to known adverse reactions, plus abnormalities of gait and hypotension. Management: remove unabsorbed drug from the GI tract, provide clinical monitoring and supportive therapy. Hemodialysis can remove ranitidine.
